task_description: I need to email our dermatologists about a new insurance pre-authorization requirement that adds 48 hours to certain procedure approvals — it affects their scheduling.

rubric_used.user_goals_summary: Writes clinic communications that prioritize patient safety and workflow continuity. Every process change is communicated with both the ideal flow and the fallback when things break. Treats email as a non-secure channel at all times.

rubric.name: Patient Flow Impact First
rubric.description: Changes are explained through their impact on patient experience and flow before the operational rationale. How many extra minutes per appointment, which rooms are affected, what the patient sees differently.

dimensions.label: The first substantive paragraph describes how the change affects patient experience or flow
Includes specific time estimates for how the change affects appointment duration or wait times
The business or compliance reason for the change appears after the patient impact, not before

rubric.name: Fallback Procedures Included
rubric.description: Every new process includes an explicit fallback for when the primary method fails. Clinical settings can't pause when technology breaks — staff need to know what to do when the system is down.

dimensions.label: Includes a specific 'if X fails, do Y instead' instruction
The fallback is a concrete procedure, not 'contact IT' or 'notify your manager'
Names the specific failure scenario the fallback addresses (system down, connectivity loss, etc.)

rubric.name: No Patient Identifiers
rubric.description: Never references patients by name in any email, even internal ones. Uses case numbers, room references, or appointment times. Email is treated as a non-secure channel regardless of policy.

dimensions.label: Does not include any patient names, initials, or uniquely identifying information
Refers to patients by case number, room number, appointment time, or generic reference
Does not include specific diagnoses, treatments, or medical details that could identify a patient in context

rubric.name: Bounded Process Steps
rubric.description: Multi-step processes use numbered steps, capped at 5. If a process needs more than 5 steps to explain in email, it needs a training session — the email should announce the training, not attempt to replace it.

dimensions.label: Processes with more than two actions use numbered steps
No process in the email exceeds 5 numbered steps
If a process is too complex for 5 steps, the email schedules training instead of attempting full documentation

rubric_used.coaching_notes: James's non-negotiable: every new process has a fallback. In clinical settings, 'the system is down' is not an edge case, it's a Tuesday. Will reject any email that names a patient or introduces a process without explaining what to do when it breaks.

**Subject:** Updated Pre-Authorization Timeline for Select Procedures – Scheduling Impact Starting [Date]

---

**To:** Dermatology Clinical Team
**From:** [Your Name/Department]
**Date:** [Date]

---

Team,

Beginning [effective date], a new insurance pre-authorization requirement will add approximately **48 hours** to approval timelines for certain procedures. Here is what this means for your scheduling and your patients.

**Impact on Patient Flow**

Patients scheduled for affected procedures will need to be contacted **at least 48 hours before their appointment** to confirm authorization status. If authorization is still pending at that point, the appointment will need to be rescheduled or converted to a consultation visit. Plan for a brief additional touchpoint — roughly **5–10 minutes per affected case** — for the front desk to communicate status updates and manage expectations before the patient arrives.

Procedure rooms and chair time should remain unaffected for authorized appointments. The change is most visible at the **scheduling and pre-visit confirmation stage**, not chairside.

This requirement is driven by updated payer policy from [Payer Name] and applies to the procedure codes listed in the attached reference sheet. Our billing team flagged this as a compliance requirement with a hard effective date.

**Updated Authorization Process**

For affected procedure codes, the workflow is:

1. At time of scheduling, flag the appointment in [EHR/scheduling system] using the "Pre-Auth Required" status.
2. Submit the authorization request to [Payer Name] within 24 hours of scheduling.
3. Monitor authorization status in [system] and update the appointment record when approval is received.
4. At the 48-hour pre-visit mark, confirm authorization status before the patient is contacted for their reminder call.
5. If authorization is not confirmed, notify the scheduling team immediately to contact the patient and offer rescheduling or a converted visit type.

**If the Authorization System Is Unavailable**

If [EHR/payer portal] is down or inaccessible, do not delay the authorization request. Use the **fax-based authorization form** (attached) and submit directly to [Payer Name] at [fax number]. Log the submission time and method in the paper tracking binder kept at the front desk. Follow up by phone with [Payer Name] at [phone number] if no confirmation is received within 24 hours of fax submission.

**Questions**

Please direct clinical workflow questions to [Clinical Lead Name] and billing or code-specific questions to [Billing Contact]. If you are unsure whether a specific procedure code is affected, check the attached list before scheduling — when in doubt, flag it.

We will monitor the first two weeks closely and will share any updates as the process settles.

Thank you,

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Contact Information]

**Subject:** Updated Pre-Authorization Timeline for Select Procedures – Scheduling Impact Starting [Date]

---

**To:** Dermatology Clinical Team
**From:** [Your Name/Department]
**Date:** [Date]

---

Team,

Starting [effective date], patients scheduled for certain procedures will receive a **different kind of pre-visit call**: rather than a standard reminder, they will be told that their appointment is pending insurance authorization and may need to change. If authorization is not confirmed by the **48-hour pre-visit mark**, they will be offered rescheduling or a converted consultation visit. From the patient's perspective, this means more uncertainty at booking and a possible second call closer to their appointment date. On the staff side, budget an extra **5–10 minutes per affected appointment** for the front desk to check authorization status and handle that outreach. Procedure rooms and chair time are unaffected for authorized visits — everything changes upstream, before the patient walks in.

This is the result of an updated payer policy from [Payer Name], effective [date], which extends approval timelines by 48 hours for the procedure codes listed in the attached reference sheet. Our billing team has confirmed there is no grace period.

**Updated Authorization Process**

For appointments involving affected procedure codes:

1. At time of scheduling, flag the appointment in [EHR/scheduling system] using the "Pre-Auth Required" status.
2. Submit the authorization request to [Payer Name] within 24 hours of scheduling.
3. Monitor authorization status in [system] and update the appointment record when approval is received.
4. At the 48-hour pre-visit mark, verify authorization is confirmed before the patient reminder call goes out.
5. If authorization is not confirmed, notify the scheduling team immediately to arrange rescheduling or a visit type conversion and contact the patient.

**If the Authorization System Is Unavailable**

If [EHR/payer portal] is down or unreachable, do not hold the request. Submit the **fax-based authorization form** (attached) directly to [Payer Name] at [fax number], and record the submission time and method in the paper tracking binder at the front desk. If no confirmation arrives within 24 hours of fax submission, call [Payer Name] directly at [phone number] to follow up.

**Questions**

Direct clinical workflow questions to [Clinical Lead Name] and billing or code-specific questions to [Billing Contact]. If you are unsure whether a procedure code is on the affected list, check the attachment before scheduling — when in doubt, flag it.

We will monitor the first two weeks closely and share updates as needed.

Thank you,

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Contact Information]
